$comment: Single source of truth for every version, milestone, contract and count quoted in the pkinative documentation. scripts/verify-docs.ts holds package.json, CITATION.cff, CHANGELOG.md and the prose to it; update this file, not the prose. verifiedOn is the date of the last documentation audit.

pkinative.npm: published from 1.0.0 by publish.yml, with npm provenance; versions below 1.0.0 are git tags only, never released

contracts.$comment: What pkinative promises, for a program to read. compatibility is the promise of SECURITY.md §Compatibility promise: three legs (ADR 0014), each naming its snapshot, the verify-docs rules that hold it, the conformance levels that verify it against a corpus, and the records that decide it; then the policies that complete it (ADR 0016, 0017, 0018), each with its records and, where one exists, the rule, registry or conformance level that holds it; then what is not promised, entry for entry with SECURITY.md. support is the runtime and compiler policy of ADR 0017. The contracts-shape rule holds the block to those files, rules and records and to SECURITY.md, both ways; it also holds runtime_dependencies to package.json, error_codes_frozen_since to docs/data/errors.frozen.json, and support to package.json engines, tsup.config.ts and the CI matrix. The snapshots and registries, not this block, carry the promised names, codes, refusals and defaults.

export-surface.promise: Every export of src/index.ts keeps its name, its kind and a compatible signature, and every PkiReasonCode keeps its name (the reason vocabulary is grow-only), for the whole major line; an addition is semver-minor.

error-vocabulary.promise: Every PkiErrorCode keeps its name and its PkiError class for the whole major line; an addition is semver-minor and carries a newer since.

decision-surface.promise: Under the default options, every refused corpus certificate stays refused with the same code for the whole major line; a new refusal is a recorded fix listed in its release note; and every corpus certificate re-encodes byte for byte from its decoded tree.

entry-points.promise: One entry point, '.', complete for the whole major line; a later minor may add a subpath export sharing one runtime chunk with it, and only a major removes one.

option-defaults.promise: The default of every option is part of the promise: changing one is semver-major, except a limit default lowered as a recorded refusal, a default added where an option had none, and the diagnostic sink.

returned-verdicts.promise: A path, revocation, CMS, timestamp, PKCS#12 or signature verdict may be corrected toward the standard, and a capability may be added, in a minor, never silently; a refusal the doctrine makes permanent is never lifted.

open-unions.promise: Every returned union may gain members in a minor, and an input reported as 'unknown' may be reported as a known kind; callers keep a default branch and branch on the positive member.

report-fields.promise: Codes, error classes, errorCode and limit names are promised, and so is the grammar of a reason or error path; messages, cited clauses, offsets, reason order and counts are not.

non-default-options.promise: Every option keeps its name, its type, its meaning and its default; what BER, strict mode, raised limits, lax PEM and the other flags accept may change in a minor, never silently.

wire-form.promise: Results are JavaScript values with bigint and Uint8Array members and no promised JSON form; the reserved convention is bigint as a decimal string and bytes as lowercase hex; the docs/data registries are additions-only and read at the git tag of a version.

corpus-repin.promise: A refusal a re-pinned corpus brings is promised from the re-pin; one the corpus calls wrong is fixed in the engine first, and a refusal the corpus drops is retired only on an accepted record.

runtime-support.promise: Node.js LTS lines with a patched floor, dropped in a minor after their end of life; TypeScript 5.0 and later on a two-year window; ES2020 for the whole major line; browsers, Deno, Bun and Workers targeted, not tested.

notPromised: error and reason message wording, and the clause a reason cites
the exact path and offset of an error or a reason, beyond the path grammar
the order of reasons, the counts a report carries, and the property order of returned objects
limit default values, which may be lowered in a minor
path, revocation, CMS, timestamp, PKCS#12 and signature verdicts, which are recorded but not frozen
runtimes beyond Node.js: Deno, Bun and browsers are smoke-tested only, Workers targeted and not executed

bundle.$comment: Byte budgets for what dist/ ships, enforced by the bundle-check gate step. verify:bundle budgets the re-minified bundle and says nothing about the shipped files. The source maps ship on purpose (tsup.config.ts sourcemap: true): a parsing library's stack traces are worth 2.6x the code when the source is MIT and already public. Every file of dist/ must have an entry, and raising one is a reviewed diff. Raised twice at 0.3.0, once per half of the milestone: for the crypto layer, measured 170281/171452/80501/80501/472771/472774; then for the build layer, measured 188455/190308/109647/109647/535650/535653. The declaration files grew 36 % against 11 % for the code, which is the surface the byte budget cannot see and declared.typeSurface can. Raised again at 0.5.0 for revocation and OCSP, measured 247184/249342/157003/157003/736695/736698 at +12 %. The declaration files are the fastest-growing artefact and declared.typeSurface is what makes that visible: 197 exports now, 115 of them types. Raised once more at 0.5.0 for the purpose check and the verify layer, measured 270984/273327/182552/182552/841166/841169 at +10 %. dist/index.d.ts is now 182552 bytes: the 1.0 trigger written down in the plan is 200000, past which subpath exports get reconsidered as a whole rather than one at a time. Raised at 0.7.0 for CMS and RFC 3161, measured 389073/391794/258879/258879/1241462/1241465 at +43 %: the largest rise so far, for a whole subsystem with its parser, builder and two verdicts. dist/index.d.ts has now passed that 200000 trigger. The decision stays where the plan put it, at 1.0 and for the whole partition at once: a subpath added now would freeze a module split before keys/ exists. Raised at 0.8.0 for PKCS#8 and PKCS#12, measured 445030/448014/294325/294325/1407559/1407562 at +14 %: keys/ now exists, so the partition the 1.0 decision will weigh is complete. At 1.0.0 dist/index.d.ts measures 307592 bytes; ADR 0016 makes this budget the next review trigger. The source maps were raised at 1.0.0 to 1530000, measured 1495196/1495199 after the pre-publication audit fixes; they ship on purpose and track the code they map.

typeSurface.$comment: The declaration file's real driver. Bytes drift with TSDoc wording, so a byte budget alone can be raised without anyone noticing that the surface doubled; these two counts cannot change by accident. Derived from docs/assets/api.json and held to it by type-surface-parity. Subpath exports were decided at 1.0 by ADR 0016: one entry point for 1.x; raising the dist/index.d.ts budget of declared.bundle reopens the question.

playgroundBundle.$comment: The playground runs a byte-for-byte copy of dist/index.js, so that it runs the build of the tree the site is published from, not the last npm release. sourceSha256 fingerprints every src/**/*.ts and tsup.config.ts; bundleSha256 and bytes describe the committed copy. All three are written by `npm run docs:playground` — never by hand — and `playground-freshness` fails when a source changed without a rebuild. maxBytes is the one hand-set field. Raised from 300000 to 400000 at 0.7.0 for the CMS and RFC 3161 layers, measured 389073: the copy is dist/index.js byte for byte, so it moves with the bundle budget above and cannot be trimmed on its own. Raised to 470000 at 0.8.0 for PKCS#8 and PKCS#12, measured 445030.

socialImages.$comment: svgSha256 is the SHA-256 of the LF-normalised SVG: it is what proves the committed PNG is not stale. Re-rasterise with the command in the SVG's header comment, then update this hash in the same commit.
